kjv: that which pertaineth unto a man
note: Hebrew keli-gever means a man's article or equipment (keli is used of tools and weapons), not simply clothing; the KJV's general phrase leaves the scope open, while many read it as male gear such as weapons.
Hebrew tiqdash means "become holy", i.e. the mixed crop is forfeited to the sanctuary; the problem is that it becomes consecrated, not that it becomes impure.

kjv: they (the elders) shall amerce him (the husband) in an hundred [shekels]
mine: they (the elders) shall fine him (the husband) a hundred shekels
note: Hebrew 'anash means to impose a fine; "amerce" is obsolete.

kjv: she hath wrought folly in Israel
mine: she has done an outrageous thing in Israel
note: Hebrew nevalah is a disgraceful, scandalous act (often sexual) that violates the community; "folly" now suggests mere foolishness.
